claims.text: High-temperature sliding induces dynamic shear that refines the near-surface grain structure of FeNiCrCoCu into an ultra-fine nanocrystalline layer.
Near-surface refinement shifts deformation from dislocation slip in coarse grains to grain-boundary-mediated sliding.
The change to grain-boundary-mediated deformation enhances wear resistance.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse grain structure.
Controlled high-temperature sliding or thermal-mechanical pre-conditioning can promote dynamic shear-induced surface grain refinement.
The relevant high-temperature operating regime is approximately 500°C to 700°C.
Sliding produces an ultra-fine nanocrystalline or dynamically amorphized surface layer at the interface.
Applied thermal and mechanical energy promotes dynamic recovery and shear deformation that refine the surface grains.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation is smoother than coarse-grained dislocation-mediated plasticity.
The proposed deformation transition suppresses highly localized defects and stress drops.
A refined, pre-conditioned coating will have a lower wear rate than the coarse-grained baseline under equivalent high-temperature sliding.
A refined, pre-conditioned coating will deform more homogeneously, with fewer and less pronounced stress-strain serrations.
The predictions hold where thermal activation permits significant dynamic grain refinement.
The predictions may fail at lower temperatures or when substrate interactions dominate deformation.
The temperature and shear thresholds needed to form the nanocrystalline layer are not yet specified.
The magnitude of the expected wear-rate reduction is not yet specified.
Failure to obtain a refined surface, or failure to obtain improved wear and deformation after pre-conditioning, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
